title: A neighbour dispute is turning hostile
lede: It started with noise, or a fence, or a parking space. Now there are notes, staring, slammed doors, maybe a camera aimed at your window. You live thirty feet from this person and cannot walk away from it.

blocks.text: It started with noise, or a fence, or a parking space. Now there are notes, staring, slammed doors, maybe a camera aimed at your window. You live thirty feet from this person and cannot walk away from it.

items: Neighbour disputes are unusual because the other party is permanent. Winning the argument is worth less than reducing the temperature.
These conflicts almost never stay about the original issue. By month three it is about disrespect, and disrespect has no settlement figure.
Whoever has the better documentation wins any formal stage — council, landlord, police, court. This is decided long before the formal stage begins.
Escalation is asymmetric: they may have far more time and far less to lose than you do.

items.detail: Every unrecorded encounter is a coin flip that can only go badly. Move everything to writing.
Date, time, what happened, duration, witnesses. Boring and consistent beats dramatic and occasional.
Specific, single-issue, no history, no adjectives. Keep a copy. This is the document that proves you tried.

items.move: Check the actual rules before asserting them
items.detail: Deeds, tenancy agreement, local noise hours, planning records. Being confidently wrong destroys your credibility for the rest of the dispute.

items.move: Bring in the neutral third party early
items.detail: Landlord, managing agent, council environmental team, or a mediation service. Early intervention is dramatically cheaper than late.

items.move: Cameras: point them at your own property only
items.detail: Recording their windows or garden converts you from complainant to respondent very quickly.

items.say: "Hi — the music on Friday and Saturday was audible in our bedroom until about 1am. Could we agree a cut-off around 11pm at weekends? Happy to talk if that does not work for you."

items.when: If they come to the door hot
items.say: "I am not going to discuss it on the doorstep. I have put it in writing and I am happy to talk when we are both calm."
Dates, durations, the requests you already made, the responses. No characterisation of them as a person.
"I will move my bin and stop parking across from your gate. I am asking for the same kind of thing back."

items: Anonymous notes. They are read as cowardice and they escalate reliably.
Involving other neighbours as a bloc. It creates a siege and hardens them permanently.
Retaliation in kind — your own noise, blocking them in. It converts a complaint into a mutual dispute and you lose your standing.
Threats you cannot execute. "I will have you evicted" from someone with no power to do so is a gift to them.
Posting about them online with identifying details.
Keep logging even during quiet periods. Gaps in a log are used to argue the problem stopped.
If a small agreement holds, acknowledge it once, briefly. Reinforcement is cheap and it works.
Price the exit honestly. Some disputes are genuinely resolved by moving, and there is no shame in that arithmetic.
Protect your sleep as a first-class priority. Sleep loss is what turns a nuisance into a health problem.

limit: Damage to property, threats to you or your family, following, or anything targeting your children makes this harassment rather than a dispute. Report it, get a crime reference number, and stop handling it neighbour-to-neighbour.
